question: At fixed arity m=3, does hybrid CDCL(T) with an F_p theory or cvc5 QF_FF achieve point-decomposition work 2^(e s) with the upper corrected 95% interval for e strictly below 0.5, while passing exact enumeration, planted, UNSAT, curve-free-null and A/A controls?

claims.text: Every completed backend row agrees with the canonical evaluator and independent group-law replay; enumerable cells have identical projected model sets.
At least one preregistered finite-field solver bundle has a complete-work exponent e whose corrected upper 95% interval is strictly below the arity-three rho crossover 0.5, outside A/A spread.
claims.if_supported: the frozen bundle advances to the separately frozen s=15..27 continuation; no asymptotic or ECDLP speedup claim
claims.if_not_supported: the frozen bundle is not advanced under the stated ladder and limits; no universal SAT or CDCL(T) impossibility claim

claims.text: The CDCL(T)/F_p bundle uses elliptic/decomposition structure beyond a support- and model-count-matched curve-free null on the tested cells.
claims.if_supported: a scoped structure effect on these predicates
claims.if_not_supported: within the matched-null distribution on these metrics; not proof that the predicate is random

claims.text: A finite solver panel proves or disproves subexponential prime-field ECDLP complexity.
claims.if_not_supported: only a proof/counterexample to the relevant theorem can decide the asymptotic statement

hypotheses.statement: The arity-three one-hot chained-S3 predicate exposes enough Boolean and finite-field structure that at least one hybrid solver bundle has complete-work exponent e below 0.5.
hypotheses.mechanism: CaDiCaL owns the one-hot Boolean skeleton while an F_p theory propagator owns field arithmetic and checked explanations; disjoint windows provide guarded three-summand rationality without an S4 expansion.

predictions.minimum_effect: upper corrected 95% interval strictly below 0.5 over the preregistered s=6..14 ladder

data_seen.measured: known-witness correctness only; no unknown solve or retired-instruction data for the declared cells
a different direct Semaev QF_BV representation

provenance.decisive_scope: the fixed-m=3, s=6..14 ladder and frozen solver/theory versions only

hypotheses.statement: Any CDCL(T) reduction is caused by elliptic/chained-S3 structure rather than one-hot and sparse-system shape alone.
hypotheses.mechanism: The curve equations and chained finite-field identities create repeated implications absent from a coefficient-randomized support-matched null.

predictions.minimum_effect: paired candidate/null median ratio at most 0.8 on the three largest rungs with corrected 95% interval below 1

provenance.decisive_scope: matched null pairs generated under this protocol

arms.description: Canonical exact two-window enumeration and projected model-set reference; expected exponent e=2 up to polynomial factors.

parameters.proof: complete projected model set where the fixed budget completes

arms.description: Polynomial IR exported to a pinned msolve F4 backend.
One-hot Boolean skeleton solved by pinned single-thread CaDiCaL with an external F_p theory propagator and checked explanation clauses.
Complete pure-CNF bit-blast retained only as an encoding-cost control; general field multiplication pays Theta(log^2 p) gates.
Finite-field SMT export solved by a pinned single-thread cvc5 binary.
Byte-identical CDCL(T) Boolean input, theory instance and seed in a fresh process/layout.
The same CDCL(T) path on instances with a hidden planted decomposition; any valid decomposition is accepted after replay.
The same CDCL(T) path on a coefficient-randomized curve-free predicate matched on field, one-hot/window shape, support graph and model class/count.

positive.expected_detection: Every planted row returns a canonical-IR-valid model whose independently extracted points sum to the public target; a miss invalidates that backend/rung's negative reading.

null_population.description: Coefficient-randomized curve-free sparse systems paired to the natural arity-three instances.
null_population.generator: Protocol-hash seeded native generator; preserve field, one-hot/window shape, variable/equation/degree multiset, monomial-support incidence graph, chart and field equations; condition on equal exact model count where enumerable and the same planted/UNSAT class otherwise.
null_population.why_n: One paired null per declared instance; test-specific power remains a freeze blocker until preflight variance is measured.
matched_on: selected chart, one-hot/window shape and field equations
exact model count on enumerable cells

factors.how: one native generator emits the semantic instance before any backend export

factors.name: curve_target_null_draw
factors.how: protocol-hash seeds, sampled independently of arm

factors.name: rung_and_target_class
factors.how: every declared arm attempts every declared cell under the same limits

factors.how: one commit and binary hash filled before freeze

factors.how: one solver version/hash/flag set per arm plus exact F_p propagator source and explanation checker, filled before freeze

factors.how: single-thread solver and environment for every arm

factors.how: masked until the frozen analysis completes

comparisons.reason: The claimed object is the complete solver/export bundle; this comparison does not attribute an effect to solver code alone.
Exact enumeration supplies the model set and the e=2 arity-three cost control; it is not the slope normalization axis.
Each candidate is fit directly against scale s and read against the arity-three rho crossover.
comparisons.threshold: upper corrected 95% interval of e strictly below 0.5

comparisons.reason: Byte-identical input/seed with a fresh process/layout.
The null is matched on field, shape, support graph and model class/count.
comparisons.threshold: paired instruction ratio <= 0.8 on the three largest rungs with corrected 95% interval below 1

comparisons.reason: Detector-power gate through the same CDCL path.
comparisons.threshold: 100% verified decompositions on completed planted rows

seed_derivation.note: Use experiment_protocol.py seeds after freeze; scratch preflight uses disjoint disclosed seeds and never the target cells.

instance_sampling.rule: For every integer s=6..14 at fixed m=3, generate eight natural, eight planted and eight exact-UNSAT instances from protocol-hash seeds before assigning arms; generate one paired matched null per instance.

blinding.how: experiment_protocol.py blind produces opaque arm labels; the original protocol/export and key are withheld from the analysis process until outputs are fixed.

power.note: Draft freeze blocker: preflight must justify power to distinguish an exponent below 0.5 from the boundary and a 1.5x paired instruction ratio under observed log-ratio variance. Passing p-value resolution alone would not establish this power.

primary.name: verified model status
primary.unit: status and canonical projected model set
primary.definition: From backend result through canonical IR evaluation, root extraction and independent group replay; enumerable cells compare the complete projected model set.

primary.name: complete retired instructions
primary.definition: First target-dependent IR compilation instruction through backend exit, model/proof extraction and independent verification; includes serialization, parsing, every theory call and explanation check, and excludes only separately reported reusable target-independent setup.

primary.name: peak resident memory
primary.definition: Maximum resident set of the wrapper and all solver descendants over the complete target-dependent interval.

primary.name: arity-three PDP complete-work exponent
primary.unit: delta log2(complete counted work) / delta s
primary.definition: Robust slope over the fixed-m=3, s=6..14 ladder, paired by instance class; no imputation for timeouts and no normalization by candidate-space size.
primary.source: analysis output from retired_instructions and instance.scale_s
primary.formula: Theil-Sen slope of log2(retired_instructions) on s

secondary.name: SAT native-work sensitivity band
secondary.definition: Decisions plus conflicts plus w times Boolean propagations, separately for w=0,0.1,1; reported beside complete work and the theory ledger, never as a replacement for either.

secondary.name: F4 solving degree
secondary.definition: Largest productive degree reported by the pinned F4 backend for the canonical polynomial system.

secondary.name: complete cold wall time
secondary.definition: The same complete target-dependent interval as retired_instructions on an L2 row; invalid after restore or below L2.

placement.memory: set from preflight with identical per-arm limit

stopping_rules.rule: Fixed design: 8 arms x 216 instances x (1 warmup + 3 measured fresh-process replicates), subject only to the same preregistered per-row timeout and memory limit; then stop.
Run the planted positive-control block first; a miss invalidates affected negative readings but all attempted rows remain in the export.
Timeouts, OOMs and nonzero solver exits are outcomes and are not retried; only recorded infrastructure failures may retry once.

invalidation_rules: a SAT witness that fails canonical evaluation or independent group replay is wrong_answer and invalidates that arm/cell
a CDCL(T) propagation or conflict with an explanation clause rejected by the independent checker is wrong_answer and invalidates that arm/cell
an UNSAT result without a checked proof object is unknown, not unsat
a natural/null pair without the preregistered shape and model-class/count match is excluded from C-structure and reported
a row without valid retired-instruction counters is excluded from instruction comparisons and reported
wall time below L2 or after restore is descriptive only with wall_valid false
a failed planted control makes the corresponding negative reading inconclusive
a row that omits theory calls or field-operation counters from the complete interval is invalid_measurement

decision_rule.text: C2 is supported within scope only when one preregistered finite-field solver bundle verifies every completed row, completes enough natural cells for the frozen power calculation without favorable-subset selection, and has a Holm-corrected upper 95% interval for e strictly below 0.5 over s=6..14, outside A/A spread and with all theory work charged. It is not advanced only when the corrected lower interval is at least 0.5 with valid controls and sufficient power. Other censoring is inconclusive. C3 is separate and requires candidate/null ratio <=0.8 on the three largest completed rungs with corrected interval below 1.
decision_rule.threshold: upper corrected interval e<0.5 for advance; lower corrected interval e>=0.5 for not-advanced; structure ratio <=0.8 for C3
decision_rule.statistic: Theil-Sen slope of log2 complete counted work on s and paired median instruction ratios, bootstrapped over held-out instances
decision_rule.interval: paired bootstrap 95% intervals, Holm-adjusted over two candidate bundles
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: instruction ratio, slope difference, and candidate/null instruction ratio, each shown against A/A spread

graphs: log2 complete counted work versus s by opaque arm, with the strict e=0.5 boundary
pure-CNF gate expansion and paired solver/F4 instruction ratios with A/A interval

inadmissible: taking affected pilot or benchmark data before the protocol is frozen and committed
changing cells, seeds, primes, curves, target class, null generator, budgets or thresholds after seeing output
comparing different selected/repeated-root charts across solver arms
omitting theory calls, field operations, explanation checks, extraction, proof, setup or verification work from one arm
calling a pure-CNF bit-blast and a CDCL(T) finite-field propagator the same solver model
treating timeout, unknown or unproved UNSAT as no solution
selecting favorable solver seeds, variable orders or propagation weights
imputing censored work to manufacture a slope
fitting the exponent against candidate-space size rather than s or using a non-strict threshold at e=0.5
reading a solver-stage result as a complete ECDLP or rho comparison
reading a finite slope as proof of subexponential complexity
